Suppose the terminal bound, after division by ZΦv(ℓ), has the form in that lemma with a fixed exponent δv. An edge may be indexed by a Z-dependent family Γe with a nonnegative measure νe, and may have the form Z Γe Z Rde Zae(ℓ,γ) |Ke,γ| re Y r=1 Nve,r Z, ℓe,r, W e,r, Ae,rt + Be,rξ θe,r dξ dνe(γ), where the child labels ℓe,r may depend on ℓ, γ. Assume uniformly in those labels that ae(ℓ, γ) + X r θe,rΦve,r (ℓe,r) − Φv(ℓ) ≤ δe, (17.4) with fixed δe, and that the child-profile bounds of the lemma hold. Assume also that for every fixed H ≥ 0, Z Γe Z Rde |Ke,γ|⟨ξ⟩H dξ dνe(γ) ≤ Ce,HZδmass e pℓe(H)(w)be(H) ⟨t⟩ce(H) , (17.5) where δmass e is fixed independently of H. When the quantities are squared Hilbert-space row norms obtained by separating a profile, this hypothesis must use the coefficient measure common to those rows. There need only be finitely many edge types at each of the finitely many depths; the cardinalities of the Γe may vary with Z. Then Nv/ZΦv(ℓ) has the conclusion of Lemma 17.3, uniformly in ℓ, with terminal exponents δv and edge exponents δe +δmass e . In particular all required seminorm and height orders are finite and independent of an external cutoff.
